entities.summary: Yvon Duhamel was a French Canadian professional motorcycle and snowmobile racer. A six-time winner of the White Trophy, the highest award in Canadian motorcycle racing, he was one of the most accomplished motorcycle racers in Canadian motorsports history. His motorcycle racing career spanned the transition from the 60 horsepower four-stroke motorcycles of the 1960s, to the 100 horsepower two-stroke motorcycles of the 1970s. Duhamel was a versatile rider competing in numerous motorcycle racing disciplines including; trials, motocross, ice racing, drag racing, flat track racing and most prominently in road racing as a member of the Kawasaki factory racing team.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Yvon Duhamel's six-time win of the White Trophy and his participation in various motorcycle racing disciplines had a significant impact on Canadian motorsports history, contributing to the country's reputation as a hub for motorcycle racing. His achievements paved the way for future generations of riders.
